findings.title: ls-tree -l's size column breaks for tree entries with a leading dash
findings.why: For tree entries git ls-tree -l emits '-' in the size column and ls-tree actually prints size only for blobs; using `{size:>8}` on the string would work but the earlier parse `_, kind, _, size = meta.split()` assumes 4 fields — actually meta has 4 fields so that's fine. The real issue is that sizes for tree entries are the literal '-' string, which still formats. Reconsider.
